sentences.text: The present misc. petition has been filed by the petitioner against the order dated 08.10.2015 passed by learned Additional Session Judge (Women Atrocities), Udaipur whereby the learned Judge dismissed the petitioner's revision petition and affirmed the order dated 08.12.2014, passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate No.3, Udaipur whereby learned trial court allowed the protest petition filed by respondent No.2 and took cognizance against the petitioner for offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC and issued arrest warrant against him.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate No.3, Udaipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners submits that initially the Police after thorough investigation submitted F.R. in the matter but subsequently the trial court took cognizance against the petitioner for the aforesaid offence and issued arrest warrant against him.

Counsel for the petitioner has made a limited prayer that the arrest warrant so issued against the petitioner may be converted (2 of 2)
[CRLMP-2974/2015] into bailable warrant and the petitioner is ready to appear before the trial court and will raise all objections at the competent stage of trial.
Learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the respondent No.2 have vehemently opposed the prayer made by the counsel for the petitioner.
I have considered the arguments advanced before me and gone through the material available on record.

sentences.text: In view of limited prayer made by the counsel for the petitioner and considering the facts that initially after thorough investigation Police submitted a final report (negative) in this case but later on, the court below has taken cognizance against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences, in these circumstances, I deem it appropriate to convert the arrest warrant so issued against the petitioner by the trial court into bailable warrant of Rs.50,000/-.
The petitioner is directed to appear before the trial court within a period of fifteen days and submit the bail bonds.
Upon submitting the bail bonds, the trial court shall release the petitioner on bail.
If the petitioner fail to appear within the stipulated period, then the trial court shall issue arrest warrant against him.
However, looking to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, liberty is granted to the petitioners to raise all the objections before the trial court at the competent stage of trial.
The misc. petition is disposed of accordingly.
Stay petition is also decided accordingly.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 189-MS/-
